updates.sentence: Sentenced to ten years, reduced to two and a half years. Confined at Fort Douglas; the archive marks Fort Leavenworth with a question mark. This is sentence length, not actual time served. Exact custody endpoints remain unresolved. expected.charges: Disobeying orders; refusal of military service (World War I court-martial of a conscientious objector)
expected.sentence: Sentenced to 20 years of hard labor in prison. Held at Fort Leavenworth. Released 1918 (Dec. 18).

updates.sentence: Twenty-year hard-labor sentence. Archive distinguishes September22,1917 draft date from Leavenworth imprisonment in1918, giving June29 with alternatives as early as June24 or late as July15. Store1918YEAR precision with those explicit bounds; January1 is a placeholder, not admission. A November2,1918 pardon and return to CampCody are not independently proved final physical release. ExistingDecember18,1918 endpoint is preserved as archival military release, without newly asserting a full uninterrupted prison span. Source: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pW6wsZo4it4CTtGmn_P-dwg1L0arJBfJEhwcIZlSZNQ/edit (Hostetler row949), linked by https://www1.swarthmore.edu/Library/peace/conscientiousobjection/WWI.COs.coverpage.htm
